public_source.legal_evidence: The Russian Wikisource page explicitly marks the literary work public domain in Russia under Article 1281 of the Civil Code and in life-plus-70-or-less jurisdictions. The work body itself is not committed by Scriptorium.

revision_family_evidence.wikisource_authorial_note: The page states that the novel was written in 1926–1927 and revised, with new chapters, in 1937.
revision_family_evidence.fantlab_work_page: FantLab notes that Tolstoy reworked the novel four times, records a new ending published in 1927, and identifies Sovetsky pisatel 1939 as the last lifetime edition.
revision_family_evidence.krestinsky_textology: FantLab-hosted Yu. A. Krestinsky commentary distinguishes four book editions (1927, 1934, 1936, 1939). It describes the 1939 Sovetsky pisatel edition as the fourth book edition, based on the 1936 text with further stylistic corrections and restoration of passages previously adapted for younger readers.
revision_family_evidence.moscow_1958_volume_textual_basis: The same Krestinsky commentary, presented under A. N. Tolstoy, Collected Works in ten volumes, volume 4, Moscow: Goslitizdat, 1958, states that the text is printed from the 1939 Sovetsky pisatel edition with checking against preceding editions. This classifies the Moscow 1958 volume-4 text as a 1939-fourth-edition-derived editorial/textual-family witness, not as a new authorial edition.
revision_family_evidence.identity_boundary: The Wikisource/az.lib transcription is not assigned to the Moscow 1958 volume or to a specific print-edition family merely because its internal 1937-revision note is compatible with late-lifetime textual history. Scriptorium requires direct evidence tying that transcription to the volume before setting bibliographic_source_identity, and separately requires evidence for FantLab's analyzer input.

bibliographic_leads.evidence: A sibling A. N. Tolstoy Wikisource text that also cites az.lib.ru identifies its text source as A. N. Tolstoy, Collected Works in ten volumes, volume 4, Emigrants. Hyperboloid of Engineer Garin, Moscow: Goslitizdat, 1958.

bibliographic_leads.source: Russian Wikisource — Случай на Бассейной улице (Толстой)
bibliographic_leads.evidence: Another sibling Tolstoy page in the az.lib.ru import lineage cites the same 1958 ten-volume collected-works volume 4 as its text source.

bibliographic_leads.source: FantLab bibliographic commentary — Ю. А. Крестинский. Гиперболоид инженера Гарина (комментарии к роману)
bibliographic_leads.evidence: The commentary identifies A. N. Tolstoy, Collected Works in ten volumes, volume 4, Moscow: Goslitizdat, 1958, and states that its Hyperboloid text is printed from the 1939 Sovetsky pisatel edition with checking against preceding editions. It therefore supplies a concrete textual-family classification for the Moscow 1958 lead.

The Russian State Library catalogs a distinct Kyiv: Goslitizdat Ukrainy, 1958, 393-page edition containing Hyperboloid of Engineer Garin and Aelita. This proves that publication year 1958 alone is not a usable edition identifier and prevents conflating the Moscow collected-works volume with another same-year edition.

public_source.bibliographic_lead_assessment: The lead is now more specific: the Moscow Goslitizdat 1958 collected-works volume 4 is textologically described as using the 1939 fourth book edition with checking against earlier editions. That narrows the edition family to test and rules out treating '1958' as a sufficient identity because another distinct 1958 Kyiv edition exists. It is still not promoted to bibliographic_source_identity: neither the Hyperboloid Wikisource page nor independently verified az.lib metadata states that this exact transcription was made from the Moscow volume.
